description.narrative: Stakeholder Effects: Improved access to affordable housing finance, including for women borrowers: IFC anticipates that the proposed investment will help ABHFL grow its affordable housing finance book, which will help address the significant shortage for affordable housing in in the country, including for women borrowers. The Project is also expected to help promote ownership of houses by women. Stakeholder Effects: Improved access to finance for MSMEs, including for women-owned MSMEs: The MSME finance gap in India is estimated to be sizeable, and for women-owned MSMEs even more so as they tend to suffer from higher perceived risk by formal financial institutions. IFC anticipates that the Project will help increase access to finance for MSMEs in India, including for women-owned MSMEs. Contribution to Market Creation: Competitiveness: IFCs support for the Project, coupled with IFCs other systematic interventions in this segment over the past few years through both debt and equity investments and advisory engagements will help promote greater competitiveness in the affordable housing sector by demonstrating the viability of providing such financing to lower-income segments, including to women borrowers.

The proposed investment envisages an Indian Rupee (INR) denominated debt of up to INR 8.3 billion (approximately US$100 million equivalent) to Aditya Birla Housing Finance Limited (ABHFL, or the Company) through senior, secured, rated, redeemable, unlisted non-convertible debentures (NCDs) for a tenor of up to five years (the Project). The Project will support the housing needs of low-income and middle-income group segments, support micro, small and medium enterprises (MSME) finance and promote affordable housing and MSME finance for women, which is still underdeveloped in India.
